clue.text: Slightly suspicious, like kedgeree?

blocks.note: first meaning: a little dubious, as an idiom
second meaning, taken literally: kedgeree is a rice dish made with smoked fish

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is literal: kedgeree, an Anglo-Indian breakfast of rice, egg and flaked fish, really does contain some fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something that seems slightly dishonest or questionable, smelling faintly wrong.

clue.text: A lone pet could be a deer

explanation.definitionFit: Antelopes are hoofed grazing animals that look much like deer, which the setter accepts loosely here.

clue.text: Like lovers or flowers?

the setter's reading: plants grow planted in a garden border of soil

explanation.walkthrough: One short phrase covers both: lovers lie between sheets, flowers grow in a garden plot.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes people lying under covers together and plants growing in a prepared garden plot.

clue.text: When Magpies and Owls have a game flavour?

explanation.definitionFit: The months each year when league matches are played, so the time these clubs take the field.

clue.text: Avenue with wise men on both sides - and brutes!

Av is the abbreviation for avenue

explanation.surface: A street flanked by philosophers, and rough types too.
explanation.definitionFit: Savages are cruel, uncivilised people, the same as brutes in plural noun form.

clue.text: Measurement when cart turns up on time

clue.text: Natural growth makes earth, for example, nearly reel

blocks.note: Earth is an example of a planet
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: A tree is a growth of nature; this one is the broad-leaved tree lining many London streets.

clue.text: Emperor's salad?

blocks.note: first meaning: the title of a Roman ruler, from Julius onward
second meaning: the romaine-and-croutons salad with anchovy dressing

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive suggests an emperor's own salad; it stands for 'is' joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman rulers took the title as a name for emperor, and a well-known lettuce dish bears the same name.

clue.text: Pompousness in showing film with wine in spiritual meeting

explanation.walkthrough: A séance is a gathering to contact the dead; the scrambled film and the wine go together into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompousness is an inflated sense of one's own worth, the same quality as being full of oneself.

clue.text: Unacceptable label attached to ducks

blocks.note: a tab is a small label or tag
a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: An offensive tag is stuck onto some waterfowl.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of nothing, so ducks are two zeros, read as letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is forbidden by social custom, beyond what people will accept.

clue.text: Change the look of modified VAT? I agree!

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Girl to lead far off

explanation.definitionFit: A paddle steamer is driven by large side or stern wheels, typical of Mississippi river traffic.

clue.text: US politicians get rising star to arrive with diamonds

explanation.walkthrough: All three pieces are joined, then the whole string reads upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Democrats are members of one of the two main American political parties.

clue.text: Drop in unannounced? Quite the reverse, as it happens!

explanation.surface: Turning up uninvited, or rather the opposite, as it turns out.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the two words swap places, not the letters: CHANCE BY becomes BY CHANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean accidentally or coincidentally, without planning, so they are interchangeable adverbs.

clue.text: Make Mum cycle, as I do in this show

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

clue.text: "Love Among the Wrinkles" attracts a second brave woman

clue.text: Meryl says: "Peter''s out of order"
